label: Bible Study
prompt: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of _____: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
verse: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
note: The motto of the whole book of Proverbs — wisdom's first lesson is reverence.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And, behold, I am with thee, and will _____ thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.
verse: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.
note: Jacob is on the run from Esau, sleeping on a stone — and God promises to keep him everywhere he goes.

label: Sunday School
prompt: In the sweat of thy _____ shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
verse: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
note: Everyone says 'by the sweat of your brow,' but the KJV puts the sweat on Adam's face.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Is there no _____ in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?
verse: Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?
note: Gilead was famous for healing resin; Jeremiah asks why, with medicine nearby, his people stay sick — the spiritual answers 'There is.'

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the _____.
verse: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.
note: The Psalter opens with a slow slide — walk, stand, sit — that ends in 'the seat of the scornful.'
